{
  "cause": "Changes in monetary policy (e.g., raising Bank Rate)",
  "effect": "Impact on inflation and the real economy",
  "linking_explanation": "Monetary policy changes take 18 to 24 months to feed through to inflation, influenced by the structure of the economy, shocks, and behavior of financial markets, firms, and households.",
  "document_reference": "Page 2, Introduction",
  "quantifications": "390 basis points increase in Bank Rate over more than a year",
  "uncertainty": "Medium"
}

{
  "cause": "Tightening in financial conditions",
  "effect": "Households cut back on consumption",
  "linking_explanation": "As financial conditions tighten, the cost of borrowing rises, and the opportunity cost of spending increases as saving rates rise, leading households to reduce consumption.",
  "document_reference": "Batch 2, Page 6",
  "quantifications": "NA",
  "uncertainty": "Low"
}

{
  "cause": "Monetary policy stance judged by the level or change of the shadow rate",
  "effect": "Overall financial conditions and the real economy",
  "linking_explanation": "The stance of monetary policy, whether judged by the level or change of the shadow rate, influences financial conditions and the real economy, but requires a relevant reference point for assessment.",
  "document_reference": "Batch 3, paragraph 1",
  "quantifications": "NA",
  "uncertainty": "Medium"
}

{
  "cause": "Higher interest rates",
  "effect": "Weigh on equity prices",
  "linking_explanation": "Higher interest rates increase the discount factor used to calculate the present value of future earnings and cash flows, leading to lower equity prices.",
  "document_reference": "Batch 4, paragraph 1",
  "quantifications": "NA",
  "uncertainty": "Low"
}

{
  "cause": "Central bank changes interest rates",
  "effect": "Changes in borrowing costs, spending, investment, and saving behavior",
  "linking_explanation": "Monetary policy affects the macroeconomy by altering interest rates, which in turn change borrowing costs and influence economic behaviors such as spending, investment, and saving.",
  "document_reference": "Page 12, Section 4",
  "quantifications": "NA",
  "uncertainty": "Low"
}

{
  "cause": "A 100 basis point monetary policy shock",
  "effect": "Persistent effect on the 1-year nominal interest rate",
  "linking_explanation": "The monetary policy shock affects the interest rate, with the effect lasting around twelve months after the shock.",
  "document_reference": "Page 14, Chart 7, top left panel",
  "quantifications": "NA",
  "uncertainty": "Low"
}

{
  "cause": "Higher degree of backward-looking inflation expectations",
  "effect": "More inflation persistence",
  "linking_explanation": "Backward-looking expectations cause inflation to persist longer even if the underlying shock remains the same.",
  "document_reference": "Batch 7, paragraph 1",
  "quantifications": "NA",
  "uncertainty": "Low"
}

{
  "cause": "Central bank raises nominal interest rates",
  "effect": "Dampening of inflation and return to baseline economic conditions",
  "linking_explanation": "In a fully forward-looking economy, raising nominal rates increases real rates, which dampens inflation and helps the economy return to baseline conditions.",
  "document_reference": "Page 18, paragraph 3",
  "quantifications": "NA",
  "uncertainty": "Low"
}

{
  "cause": "Agents increasingly being backward-looking in their expectations formation",
  "effect": "Monetary policy needs to be increasingly restrictive to return the inflation rate to target",
  "linking_explanation": "Backward-looking expectations formation makes it harder for monetary policy to influence inflation, requiring more aggressive policy measures to achieve targets.",
  "document_reference": "Page 20, paragraph 1",
  "quantifications": "NA",
  "uncertainty": "Medium"
}

{
  "cause": "Monetary policy announcements",
  "effect": "Firm expectations",
  "linking_explanation": "Monetary policy announcements can influence the expectations of firms regarding future economic conditions, which in turn can affect their investment and pricing decisions.",
  "document_reference": "Di Pace, F., G. Mangiante and R. Masolo (2023). Do firm expectations respond to monetary policy announcements?, Staff Working Paper No. 1014.",
  "quantifications": "NA",
  "uncertainty": "Medium"
}

{
  "cause": "Central bank increases policy interest rates",
  "effect": "Reduction in household borrowing and consumption",
  "linking_explanation": "Higher interest rates raise borrowing costs, which discourages households from taking loans and reduces spending.",
  "document_reference": "Ramey, V. A. (2016). 'Chapter 2 - Macroeconomic shocks and their propagation in Taylor, J. B. and H. Uhlig (2016) Handbook of Macroeconomics, 2, pp. 71-162.",
  "quantifications": "NA",
  "uncertainty": "Low"
}
